Every existing Control Panel trigger is re-homed onto its screen, the Control Panel becomes the index (scenario jumps, clock and reset stay there), and the HL7/FHIR tooling gets interim Future-scope badges plus an S1 caveat.

phases.title: AA fee as its own monthly invoice
phases.goal: Step 1, re-greened on its own: stop netting the 5% AA fee from the ACCPAY, so the payable equals the receivable and a part payment releases exactly the amount received (US-10.2.1); reseed billing history, remove the Xero simulator's fee block and web Payments' fee columns, and re-baseline the S3 figures. Each fee invoice has its own number, billing case and simulated ACCREC against the anaesthetist's Xero contact; it is always a separate invoice paid into AA's own account, never netted against payables (Greg, 2026-10-02: trust law). The BCTI count runs through one pure, tested function (BCTIs for an anaesthetist in a month), the only place the count is made. Later phases that add invoices (22, 36, 38b, 39, 39b) feed it and must keep it the only count. Admin and web Accounts show the fee invoice paid or unpaid, and Xero pair records carry the invoice number and reference. phases.title: Slot and List split
phases.goal: Introduce a Slot record for each active anaesthetist, day and session from the anaesthetist's start date (a new start-date field on the anaesthetist and the Add flow, editable afterwards), with a deterministic id, holding the availability status and default times. Per OQ-64 (answered), a Slot is a status container a List goes into, every Slot is stored across the horizon, and the status is the one mechanism the calendar edits (Phase 29), not a second record reconciled into Lists. Generation follows US-01.1.1 (Confirmed): every new Slot starts free (the RNG fill of private, public and unavailable sessions goes, including on rolled days and new anaesthetists), only active anaesthetists get Slots, then the anaesthetist's own calendar is painted, then the surgeons' recurring bookings (OQ-81 part 1, settled in the room; a recurring booking on an unavailable Slot becomes a Draft List in Phase 31). The horizon is a setting, four months in current practice (FT-01.1): shortening it drops far-edge days and extending it fills them. The List becomes its own record with a slotId, created on assignment: by office assignment from a free Slot (which requires a surgeon and a hospital, creates an ACTIVE List, the state 15b named, and shows Phase 17's not-preferred warning) or by the recurring-booking projection; once a List is in a Slot, the List shows in place of the status. The displayed status derives from the Slot plus the attached List, independent of bookings, and matches across mobile, web, admin and the availability finders (US-01.4.2), so a phone-booked session no longer reads Free. The admin availability finders list available anaesthetists through Phase 17's helper, ordered by priority tier and shuffled within a tier, with not-preferred pairings apart (US-01.3.5, US-01.3.6); the anaesthetists' own finders on mobile and web are never tier-ordered and show no preferences. The Admin Day grid's roster comes from the anaesthetist master, so added anaesthetists appear. Default AM and PM times and the horizon come from one schedule-settings record. Reassign moves a List between Slots, and the vacated Slot returns to free. Re-point the canvas generator, clock roll-forward, selectors, Admin Day grid, mobile schedule, web availability and registry context. The word 'slot' never reaches app copy (OQ-64): say session, AM or PM. Bump PERSIST_VERSION (15b already renamed the assigned List's state to ACTIVE).
phases.delivers: A Slot record for every active anaesthetist's session across a configurable horizon, free by default, holding availability and default times. A List with its own id, created on assignment and shown in place of the status. Status independent of bookings in all three apps and the finders, the admin finder ordered by tier with not-preferred pairings apart. Added anaesthetists on the Admin Day grid. phases.title: Availability calendar and status master
phases.goal: Anaesthetists keep their sessions' availability from a calendar on mobile and web, weeks ahead: a session is free by default and they change it (for example on holiday or unavailable), set days off ahead, add a recurring series, and edit or delete one instance. The calendar edits the Slot status directly (one mechanism), which also brings the web app to parity. Pressing Free on a booked session no longer raises a false conflict. Per OQ-64 (answered), the Slot status set becomes a user-maintained master list instead of a TypeScript union: a fixed internal ID that rules read, an editable label and a colour mapped to design tokens, and new statuses added without code (US-01.2.2). The Slot's availability status is separate from the List's state (DRAFT, ACTIVE, SUBMITTED, AUTHORISED; US-01.2.2 since 2026-10-07): the status master never holds a List state. It is seeded with the owner's starting values (free, on holiday, unavailable; several kinds of unavailable may be added for information, with the same effect), while a session holding a List shows the List in its place with the design's List colours. Until Phase 32 adds the return-or-assign choice, marking unavailable a session that holds a List keeps today's conflict flag, but the false 'the office was notified' copy goes.
